$comment: Explicitly accepted npm audit findings. Consumed by scripts/audit.mjs.
- The audit threshold stays at --audit-level=high. Never lower it to make a
finding disappear; add a reviewed entry here instead, or fix the dependency.
- Every entry needs an advisory ID, a justification grounded in why the code
is not reachable or not exploitable HERE, and a reviewBy date.
- The audit script FAILS once reviewBy has passed. That is deliberate: an
accepted risk with no expiry is an ignored risk.
- Entries that no longer match any finding are reported as stale. Remove them.

allow.title: DeepmergeTS has stack exhaustion when merging recursive object graphs
justification: Reachable only through the Prisma CLI (prisma -> @prisma/config -> deepmerge-ts),
which is build-and-migration tooling. It is not part of the @prisma/client query
Verified not shipped: after `npm run build`, none of deepmerge-ts, @prisma/config,
or the prisma CLI appear anywhere under .next/standalone, which is what the
Dockerfile copies into the production image.
It appears in the production dependency tree at all only because @prisma/client
declares `prisma` as an OPTIONAL PEER dependency, which npm installs by default.
That is why `npm audit --omit=dev` still reports it despite prisma being a
Triggering it requires attacker-controlled input to a Prisma config merge. Prisma
config comes from files in this repository, not from user input, so there is no
path from a faculty member or an anonymous visitor to this code.
The only remediation npm offers is downgrading to prisma@6.12.0, which is older
than the client we generate against and fixes nothing that is actually reachable.
